My capsule wardrobe

Kimawashi

Saved in this browser

Relaxed layering with French basics, British trad and American workwear, in a rich, warm palette. Start with the look, then browse the pieces and outfits.

The look

Relaxed, layered and lived-in. Think a girl in loafers and colored socks, a men's shirt under a cardigan, a wide skirt or cords, and a tote that has clearly been everywhere. Pieces are simple and classic, but the way they're mixed is personal: masculine with feminine, sporty with sweet, vintage with new. Nothing looks too polished or too trendy.

The magazines

FUDGE is a monthly published by Sanei since 2002. It calls itself a fashion and culture magazine for girls, and it leans on Paris and London street style: French casual and British trad pieces like denim, loafers and trench coats, finished with glasses or a scarf, plus vintage finds and street snaps from cities around the world. The tone is grown-up but still playful and cute. Its core readers are in their 20s and 30s.

CLUÉL is a monthly from THE BOOKS Publishing built around two words, 上品 (refined) and 上質 (quality). Its editorials are often shot on location in European cities with foreign models, and its styling mixes simple casual, trad and boyish, menswear-inspired pieces. It favors timeless basics over trends and pays close attention to bags, shoes and accessories. Readers are mostly in their 20s and 30s, with plenty older.

Both have menswear sister titles, MEN'S FUDGE and CLUÉL homme, which shows in how often the women's pages borrow from men's wardrobes.

The culture around it

  • Trad and Ivy. Japan has loved American Ivy League and British country clothing since the 1960s. Oxford shirts, loafers, duffle coats, cable knits and tartan read as classic here, not costume.
  • French casual. フレンチカジュアル is its own style category: simple basics, a few good pieces, and a relaxed, unbothered attitude.
  • Vintage. 古着 (furugi, secondhand clothing) shops are a big part of street style. A worn-in jacket or a thrifted skirt is a point of pride.
  • Select shops. Multi-brand stores that mix their own lines with imported and vintage pieces shape much of this look, and magazines feature their staff's outfits often.
  • Kimawashi. Japanese magazines regularly run 着回し features that build a month of outfits from a small set of pieces. That's the same idea as this capsule.

In an international context

Outside Japan, this look sits where several familiar Western styles meet, filtered through a Japanese eye for fit, layering and detail.

  • Preppy and Ivy, via Japan. In 1965 the Japanese photobook Take Ivy documented students at American Ivy League campuses, and Japanese brands and magazines went on to study and refine that style for decades. Writer W. David Marx calls this Ametora (American traditional), and argues Japan helped preserve classic American clothing when America itself moved on. Oxford shirts, loafers and chore jackets here come from that lineage.
  • British heritage. Tartan, duffle coats, fisherman knits and lace-up boots are borrowed from British country and school dressing.
  • The "French girl" look. The simple basics, minimal makeup and relaxed attitude overlap with the Parisian style that Western media also celebrates.
  • Close cousins. Fans of dark academia (tweed, tartan, knits and loafers in warm browns) or heritage workwear will recognize a lot here. The Japanese version is softer and more playful, with colored socks, gathered bags and sweet collars.
  • Copenhagen street style. The same habit of pairing sporty sneakers and nylon bags with feminine skirts and knits.
  • Not Harajuku. Internationally, Japanese fashion is often pictured as bold Harajuku styles like Lolita or decora. This is the opposite end: the everyday, grown-up casual that most stylish people in Japanese cities actually wear. Its nearest Japanese relative is mori girl, the layered, natural-fabric "forest girl" look of the late 2000s.
  • Capsule wardrobes. The Western capsule wardrobe idea, popularized by London boutique owner Susie Faux in the 1970s and Donna Karan's "Seven Easy Pieces" in 1985, matches the kimawashi tradition of Japanese magazines: a few well-chosen pieces worn many ways.

Palette

Rich, warm and dark. Chocolate, cream, beige, camel, deep navy and denim make the base, with black kept for formal pieces and legwear. Pick one accent per outfit. Your palette lives on the Style tab, where you can change it. Near your face, choose cream over stark white, and chocolate or deep navy over black. Deep navy looks best with camel, rust or cream, just like the tartan.

Styling rules

  • One sporty piece per outfit, like chunky sneakers or the nylon bag, balanced with something soft or classic: a skirt, a knit or a collar.
  • Let layers peek out: a collar over a sweater, a tee under a pinafore.
  • Socks are part of the outfit, so pick them on purpose.
  • Keep bags and shoes in chocolate, black or cream so everything mixes.
  • Skip horizontal stripes; solids, cords, cables and checks carry the texture instead.
  • Buy secondhand where you can. Vintage denim, knits and coats suit this look best.

Outfit formulas

Four easy ways this capsule goes together.

Seasons and smart days

  • Hot, humid days: linen, sandals and a sun umbrella do most of the work.
  • Cold days: layer a turtleneck under knits, add tights under skirts, and finish with the duffle coat.
  • Rainy days: the umbrella doubles for sun and rain, so there's no need for a rain jacket.
  • Smart days: the blazer and tailored trousers dress up any outfit while keeping the relaxed look. Filter Outfits by Work to see them.
  • Very formal days: the dark suit jacket and trousers with plain black pumps.

Hair, makeup, skincare and everyday life, from what FUDGE has featured in 2025 and 2026. CLUÉL sticks almost entirely to clothes, so this side mostly comes from FUDGE. Plus shopping words and clothing care. The Watch links open a video search, in Japanese and in English.

Hair

  • The cut of the moment is a layered bob (レイヤーボブ), usually with face-framing layers (顔まわりレイヤー) that are allowed to fall loosely around the face. Variations: a rounded diamond shape (ひし形), soft wolf layers at the nape (襟足ウルフ), or a light tousled perm (クシャパーマ).
  • Bangs with a bob (前髪ありボブ) are chosen to suit the face shape rather than cut straight across by default.
  • For autumn and winter 2026, Tokyo stylists rank layers, the hush cut (ハッシュカット, a soft, choppy layered cut from Korea) and layered bobs as the top cuts.
  • Color leans warm. Chestnut browns, mauve chocolate (モーヴショコラ) and bordeaux or wine (ボルドー) are all current. Natural, uncolored hair fits right in too: the cut does most of the work. Mint and olive beiges are also trending, but they're the cooler end.

Things to say at a salon:

  • 顔まわりにレイヤーを入れたレイヤーボブにしたいです。 (I'd like a layered bob with face-framing layers.)
  • シースルー前髪にしたいです。 (I'd like see-through bangs.)
  • カラーはせず、地毛のままでお願いします。 (No color, please. I'd like to keep my natural hair.)

Makeup

  • Skin: thin and glowy (薄膜ツヤ肌), with a blurring powder only where you need it.
  • Brows: fluffy and brushed up (ふさふさ眉) with brow mascara in a reddish brown (赤みブラウン), which suits warm coloring.
  • Lips in autumn and winter: deep but soft. FUDGE's picks ran from rose brown and bordeaux to brick and terracotta; the pick here is mocha, a soft pinky brown that stays warm without turning orange. Wear it in a velvety soft matte or a glossy, balm-like finish rather than a dry matte, applied straight from the bullet and blotted for a lived-in look.
  • Lips in spring and summer: peach and nude, slightly overlined and blotted.
  • Cheeks: a soft peach or rose-brown, sheer and diffused, patted in with a finger or brushed lightly upward.
  • Match the lip to the outfit, the way FUDGE does: mocha with camel, chocolate, cream and the burgundy cardigan; a deeper rose brown with deep navy or the tartan; peach with denim and linen.

Skincare

FUDGE organizes skincare by what your skin needs rather than by long routines:

  • Cleanse gently and don't strip the skin.
  • Calm and cool skin after heat or sun.
  • Exfoliate gently, once or twice a week, not every day. Their pick was mild acids such as BHA or PHA. Patch-test anything new.
  • Protect from UV every day, and remember hair and body too.
  • Brighten and moisturize, for example with vitamin C derivatives or plant oils.
  • Prep before makeup (プレベースメイク) so a thin base looks smooth. This was one of 2025's big beauty words in Japan.

Clothing care

A capsule is worn often, so a little care keeps it looking good for years. Always check the care label first. Japanese labels use the same symbols as international ones.

  • Knits: wash by hand in cool water with a wool detergent (おしゃれ着洗い), press the water out without wringing, and dry flat. Fold them instead of hanging. For pilling (毛玉), use a fabric shaver or a sweater comb, and give knits a day of rest between wears.
  • Corduroy: wash inside out on a gentle cycle. Smooth the ribs by hand while it's damp, and steam from the back instead of pressing it flat.
  • Linen: wash gently and hang it while it's still damp. A few wrinkles are part of the look; iron while damp if you want it crisp.
  • Denim: wash rarely, inside out and cold, and hang to dry so the color lasts.
  • The duffle coat: brush it after wearing (ブラッシング), air it out before putting it away, and store it on a wide hanger. Clean it the way its label says.
  • Leather shoes and bags: wipe off dust, condition now and then, and stuff bags with paper to keep their shape. Rest shoes a day between wears and use shoe trees if you have them.
  • Nylon bags: spot-clean with a damp cloth and a little mild soap.

Living

FUDGE's lifestyle pages keep coming back to the same small pleasures:

  • Books, films, music and art, with recommendations in every issue, plus small independent shops like secondhand bookshops and flower shops.
  • Handmade and vintage: ceramics, knitting, flowers and flea markets. FUDGE runs its own market with vintage, handmade goods and ceramics.
  • Moving, gently: FUDGE has its own running club, and pickleball showed up at its 2026 market.
  • Travel: weekends in Paris, London and Finland, planned around what to wear.
  • Home: interiors in the spirit of "living my own way" (私らしく暮らす).

Ideas to try: a long walk that ends at a secondhand bookshop or a flower shop; a month of kimawashi with the 30-day challenge on the Outfits tab; a flea market or vintage shop to find one secondhand piece; a film night at home with a new playlist or a book from the magazine's picks.

Current vs dated

  • Current: layered bobs and face-framing layers; warm or natural browns; thin, glowy skin; full, natural brows; soft-matte or balm lips in browns like mocha; sheer peach or rose-brown cheeks; gentle, need-based skincare.
  • Looking dated: a plain one-length bob with no layers; heavy, dry matte lips; makeup advice written around wearing masks.

Trends move every season. These are based on FUDGE features and stylist surveys up to autumn 2026.
